title: Trump Orders Pentagon to Cut South Korea Military Drills, Cites Kim Jong Un Ties
excerpt: The order to 'substantially reduce' Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises came hours before they were set to begin, prompting Seoul to push for stronger independent defense.
body:
• President Trump instructed the Pentagon to 'substantially reduce' annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises with South Korea, citing costs and Seoul's refusal to assist with Iran.
  • The Ulchi Freedom Shield drills — involving about 18,000 South Korean troops — began as scheduled on Monday despite Trump's order, though it remains unclear if they have been scaled back.
  • South Korean President Lee Jae Myung responded by calling for stronger independent defense capabilities and faster progress on the country's nuclear-powered submarine program.
  • North Korea had condemned the drills as more provocative than last year's exercises and warned it would strengthen its nuclear deterrent.

Trump's Order and the Iran Connection

President Donald Trump on Sunday instructed the Pentagon to "substantially reduce" joint military exercises with South Korea, upending a cornerstone of the seven-decade-old alliance just hours before annual drills were set to begin.

https://x.com/htTweets/status/2089569759822237764

Writing on Truth Social, Trump said he was "not happy" that the United States had agreed to participate in the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises, which run through August 27 and involve roughly 18,000 South Korean military personnel.

"These exercises are not only costly... but send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile, to a Country that, as long as Donald J. Trump has been President, has been unthreatening and respectful."

— President Donald Trump, on Truth Social

Trump linked his decision to Seoul's stance on the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. "I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, 'No thanks!'" he wrote, adding the parenthetical "while somewhat unrelated."

He also highlighted his "very good relationship" with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and said Kim had responded to his outreach, though he provided no details on the nature of that communication.

Drills Proceed Despite the Order

South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff told Reuters the Ulchi Freedom Shield drills started on Monday as scheduled, though officials declined to comment on Trump's remarks. The exercises were designed this year to incorporate training against drones, GPS jamming, and cyberattacks — threats reflecting North Korea's evolving military capabilities.

A Pentagon spokesperson referred questions to the White House, which did not immediately clarify how or when the exercises would be curtailed. The practical impact of Trump's order remains uncertain.

A US defense official noted the drills were focused on threats to the Korean Peninsula and the defense of South Korea, highlighting that North Korean soldiers who fought alongside Russia in Ukraine had brought back battlefield lessons that made readiness exercises more important, not less.

Seoul Pushes for Self-Reliance

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung used a cabinet meeting on Tuesday to call for stronger independent defense capabilities, framing the alliance and self-reliance as mutually reinforcing rather than contradictory.

"A strong alliance makes the foundation of security stronger, and strengthening our own capabilities increases our value and necessity as an ally," Lee said, according to Reuters.

Lee called for faster progress on South Korea's nuclear-powered submarine program and for developing officers capable of conducting integrated operations across modern battlefields. He also said Seoul should proceed without disruption on the planned transfer of wartime operational control from the United States.

At a National Security Council meeting, Lee emphasized that the civil-defense exercises held alongside the military drills were purely defensive in character. "South Korea had no intention of using the exercises to attack North Korea or raise tensions on the Korean Peninsula," the presidential Blue House said in a statement.

North Korea's Warnings and Broader Stakes

North Korea had condemned the drills before Trump's announcement, calling them more provocative than last year's exercises. State media outlet KCNA cited a foreign ministry spokesperson warning that US-Japan-South Korea military cooperation was turning into "a nuclear alliance" and that Pyongyang would respond with a new level of deterrent.

Days before the exercises began, North Korea fired a ballistic missile from its eastern coast toward the Sea of Japan — the second such launch in recent days, according to South Korean and Japanese military officials.

Lieutenant General Joseph Jarrard of US Northern Command warned last week that North Korea had successfully tested intercontinental ballistic missiles with "enough boost to deliver a nuclear payload anywhere in North America."

Economic Tensions Underneath

Analysts say Trump's frustration extends beyond military cost-sharing. The countries signed a trade deal last year under which Seoul committed to invest $350 billion in exchange for lower auto tariffs, but South Korea has not announced details of its investment plan, according to Reuters.

Jenny Town, head of the Stimson Center's 38 North program, said the move may be aimed at creating diplomatic space with Pyongyang, "although the haphazard nature of this move is unlikely to make much of an impression."

Victor Cha, head of the Korea program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, offered another lens: "Trump wants to engage Kim as a way to impede the Russia-NK ties" — a strategic calculation given Pyongyang's deepening military relationship with Moscow.
nri_angle: The move raises broader questions about US alliance commitments in Asia that affect Indian strategic calculations and regional stability.
